answer.rationale: Finance mandate of 18% cost reduction with incumbent refusal to renegotiate forces a decision. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor executed cleanly on onboarding and invoicing accuracy in a prior switch, directly addressing execution risk. memory_c4 context shows negotiation recovered margin but incumbent has already refused this cycle, closing that path. Switching to the low-cost vendor meets the mandate alone per current quote. However, assembly line is at 94% utilization with no buffer—this creates material delivery risk if the vendor onboarding encounters the delays that memory_c1 avoided with incumbents. The 14-day contract expiration window is tight for vendor validation. Verification of memory_c2 (prior successful switch) and memory_c4 (failed negotiation this cycle) will confirm whether low-cost vendor's prior performance extends to current scale, and whether negotiation truly is closed. Standard experiment scale with close monitoring during the 90-day ramp to detect margin drift or delivery friction early, before full dependency.
